name: Inari Saami
sweep_summary: One title-hit for Inari Saami: Wiklund 1896, Entwurf einer urlappischen Lautlehre (MSFOu X). fetched sources open copies from Fenno-Ugrica (handle 10024/89839, ABBYY text layer) and archive.org (suomalaisugrila04seurgoog); both with a manifest (also listing the 9/16 files already in the folder). The 'Accent' chapter (p. 123, page image checked) says word accent is on the first syllable in all present-day Saami dialects and therefore in Proto-Saami, with secondary-accent position undetermined; it is a pan-Saami/Proto-Saami statement with no Inari-specific accent data, so relevance is other-language-or-variety and it merely confirms the catalog's fixed-dominant (initial) coding. Nothing left to acquire from this item (priority none). The catalog record's deciding citation is still empty (Wikipedia-sourced); the recommended deciding source remains Äimä 1918 §54.1 p. 80 ('Der hauptton oder gravis liegt bei isoliert ausgesprochenen Wörtern auf der 1. silbe'), read and filed in the 9/16 pass ( / Aima1914 page images in the same folder), with Wiklund 1896:123 usable as family-level corroboration. all lookups were done with direct fetches (archive.org API, Fenno-Ugrica, HathiTrust API — the OCLC probe returned no HathiTrust record).

new_statements.quote: Der wortaccent liegt in allen jetzigen lappischen dialekten überall auf der ersten silbe des wortes. Wir können also schliessen, dass er auch in urlappischer zeit denselben platz gehabt hat, gewiss schon in der allerältesten urlappischen periode, da, wie bekannt, auch das finnische den wortaccent auf die erste silbe legt. In einem mehrsilbigen worte haben weiter ein oder vielleicht mehrere nebenaccente existieren müssen. Auf welcher silbe sie ihren platz gehabt haben, kann noch nicht ermittelt werden.
new_statements.translation: In all present-day Lappish [Saami] dialects the word accent lies everywhere on the first syllable of the word. We may therefore conclude that it had the same place in Proto-Lappish times too, certainly already in the very oldest Proto-Lappish period, since, as is well known, Finnish also places the word accent on the first syllable. In a polysyllabic word there must further have been one or perhaps several secondary accents. On which syllable they had their place cannot yet be determined.
new_statements.citation: Wiklund, Karl Bernhard. 1896. Entwurf einer urlappischen Lautlehre. I. MSFOu X. Helsingfors.
new_statements.locator: 'Accent', p. 123 (Fenno-Ugrica pdf page 135; page image verified)
new_statements.reading: Blanket family-level claim (1896) that every living Saami dialect, hence Inari Saami, has fixed initial word stress, with secondary-stress placement left open. It is consistent with the catalog's fixed-dominant/initial coding but is neither Inari-specific nor first-hand (Wiklund's own fieldwork was Lule Saami; his Inari data are second-hand). The only item in this sweep, so it is the best statement read today, but it should be cited only as corroboration.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Inari Sami language', Phonology/Prosody section, re-read 2026-08-31
sources.quote: Inari Sami, like the other Samic languages, has fixed word-initial stress. Words are furthermore divided into feet, usually consisting of two syllables each, and with secondary stress on the first syllable of every foot.

sources.citation: Äimä, Frans. 1918. Phonetik und Lautlehre des Inarilappischen. I. Beobachtungsphonetik und deskriptive Lautlehre. Mémoires de la Société Finno-Ougrienne 42. Helsinki: SUS. (Fenno-Ugrica handle 10024/89873)
sources.quote: §54.1 (p. 80): 'Der hauptton oder gravis liegt bei isoliert ausgesprochenen Wörtern auf der 1. silbe.' p. 81: in a Sprechtakt only the 1st syllable is hauptbetont; in lively speech after a main-stressed monosyllable the 2nd syllable may exceptionally outrank the 1st ('durch rhythmische gründe bedingt'). §54.2 (p. 81-83): 'Der starke nebenton, gravior, scheint früher in der regel auf den ungeraden inlautssilben gelegen zu haben'; the rule still holds where original syllable count is preserved, but syncope, apocope and contraction yield present-day patterns with strong secondary stress on the 2n

sources.citation: Türk, Helen, Pärtel Lippus, Merit Niinemägi, Karl Pajusalu & Pire Teras. 2022. The durational structure of tetrasyllabic words in Inari Saami. Proc. Speech Prosody 2022, Lisbon, 891-895. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2022-181
sources.quote: 'Words are mostly divided into feet following a trochaic pattern with a stressed initial syllable and a following unstressed syllable. Trisyllabic words in Inari Saami form a trisyllabic foot with two unstressed syllables following the primary stressed initial syllable.' Abstract: tetrasyllables 'are mainly divided into two disyllabic feet where the first two syllables form a primary stressed foot and the secondary stress is on the third syllable. However, a pattern where a trisyllabic foot is followed by a stressed fourth syllable also occurs' (contracted -eijee agent nouns).
sources.note: Most recent acoustic study; explicit English statement of trochaic initial stress and the two tetrasyllabic secondary-stress patterns; quotable replacement for the Wikipedia sentence.

sources.citation: Bye, Patrik, Elin Sagulin & Ida Toivonen. 2009. Phonetic duration, phonological quantity and prosodic structure in Inari Saami. Phonetica 66(4): 199-221. doi:10.1159/000298583 (author copy from carleton.ca/toivonen)
sources.quote: 'Main stress was still assigned to the first syllable, which in trisyllabic words formed a degenerate foot of its own ... Proto-Inari Saami *(σ́)(σ̀σ) > Inari Saami (σ́)(σ̀) ... The cumulative effect of metrical restructuring and apocope was thus the introduction of a new contrast that turned on the presence versus absence of a word-final monosyllabic foot: (σ́σ) vs. (σ́)(σ̀)' -- i.e. primary stress fixed initial; foot structure / secondary stress is lexically-morphologically specified, not purely alternating binary feet.
sources.note: Modern instrumental + metrical analysis stating main stress on the first syllable and showing secondary-stress/foot structure is contrastive ((σ́σ) vs (σ́)(σ̀)), which corrects the Wikipedia 'every foot two syllables' simplification.

sources.citation: Türk, Helen, Pärtel Lippus, Karl Pajusalu & Pire Teras. 2020. Temporal patterns of geminates in Inari Saami trisyllabic words. Proc. Speech Prosody 2020, Tokyo, 81-85. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2020-17
sources.quote: Quantity 'is manifested in the intervocalic position between the stressed and unstressed syllables' of the disyllabic word; vowel length distinctive only in stressed syllables. Presupposes initial stress; no explicit placement rule.

sources.citation: Türk, Helen. 2019. Consonantal quantity systems in Estonian and Inari Saami. PhD dissertation, University of Tartu (Dissertationes Philologiae Uralicae). hdl:10062/64625
sources.quote: Geminates 'occur in the intervocalic position at the boundary of stressed and unstressed syllables of disyllabic feet'; reports Bye et al.'s suggestion that in VVC'CVC words 'the second syllable bears secondary stress'. No explicit primary-stress placement statement.
